message: SP-45 — Two rules the model must not break. Money comes from the summary snapshot, never live catalogue rates. And every money measure filters to month rows.
SP-46 — Why the month filter specifically?
SP-46 — The summary table holds clipped week rows alongside month rows. Without the filter every money figure double-counts and the report is confidently wrong, which is worse than blank.
SP-46 — Understood. I will put the filter in the base measure so no page-level visual can forget it.
SP-44 — Queries are per table and select only the columns the report uses. A schema change then shows up as a named missing column instead of a silently empty visual.
SP-47 — Cost by shift type and cost by manager pages are done, plus a drill-through to the day detail for one employee month.
SP-48 — Writing the rebuild runbook. Assumption is a machine with nothing installed and no account. Divya, does the file need a live connection to demo?
SP-48 — No, the data is cached in the file. Desktop is free and no sign-in is needed to open it. A demo needs one install and nothing else.

SP-91 — Starting an August reconciliation before handover, report totals against what the Manager Approval widget shows for the same month. If those two disagree I would rather find it than the client.
SP-91 — First pass is out by roughly double on every reportee. Checking my measures before I go blaming the data.
SP-46 — Roughly double is the clipped week rows counting alongside the month rows. Check the period filter is actually on the measure that visual is reading.

That was it. One visual was reading a measure that bypassed the base filter. Exactly the failure SP-46 exists to prevent, and it took ten minutes rather than a day because we already knew where to look.
August reconciled across four reportees. Report and widget agree to the rupee. Closing SP-91.
